goals: PRIMARY (infeasible): compute hillslope-to-stream travel times with lateral flow convergence and inter-hillslope groundwater exchange
FALLBACK (partial): characterize how vertical water partitioning and local recharge/drainage flux vary by hillslope position, to generate boundary fluxes for a future lateral/travel-time model
key_processes: lateral subsurface flow / convergence along flowpaths (NOT representable in 1-D ELM)
groundwater exchange between neighboring columns (NOT representable)
flow routing and travel-time / transit-time computation (no routing capability)
vertical partitioning: ET, surface runoff, sub-surface drainage QDRAI, soil moisture (representable per-column)

model_choice.rationale: ELM single-column 1-D can only resolve vertical fluxes per isolated column; it cannot represent lateral routing, convergence, or inter-column groundwater exchange, which are the core of the request.
model_choice.coupling_note: Travel times and lateral convergence would require ELM per-position drainage/recharge to drive a lateral subsurface flow model (PFLOTRAN) plus a particle-tracking / transit-time solver. ELM->PFLOTRAN coupling and travel-time routing are not implemented — listed in requires_capabilities.

answerable: per-position vertical water partitioning (ET, surface runoff, QDRAI, soil moisture) at ridge/mid-slope/toe columns under uniform forcing
how local recharge/drainage flux varies with soil texture across the domain

not_answerable.why: no flow-routing or transit-time capability; single-column ELM produces no connected flowpath

not_answerable.aspect: lateral flow convergence along topographic flowpaths
not_answerable.why: ELM columns are hydraulically isolated 1-D; no lateral flux exchange exists
not_answerable.needs: laterally-connected subsurface flow model (e.g. PFLOTRAN) coupled to ELM

not_answerable.aspect: groundwater exchange between neighboring hillslope positions
not_answerable.why: no inter-column water-table communication in single-column ELM
not_answerable.needs: ELM->PFLOTRAN coupling with a shared regional water table

not_answerable.why: forcing is uniform; no elevation-downscaled forcing, so elevation/climate effect is not isolable from soil

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (fallback only — generates per-position vertical boundary fluxes, NOT travel times)
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 hillslope positions x 3 elevation bands = 9 representative columns to span topographic position and the wide 352-1977 m range; soil enters via the raster the expander samples at each point. This is the minimum to characterize position-dependent vertical fluxes; it does NOT and cannot resolve travel times or lateral exchange.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate along representative hillslope transects (ridge->toe) and oversample toe-slope/riparian zones where groundwater-soil-moisture exchange would matter most in a future coupled model; span the elevation gradient.
sampling_strategy.replication: None — single representative column per position x elevation cell; N kept small because these are boundary-flux generators, not a validated result.

sampling_plan.reason: Upslope recharge-source columns: vertical drainage flux that would feed downslope lateral flow in a coupled model.
Transmission-zone columns spanning elevation; local partitioning between bands, no lateral transfer represented.
Convergence/discharge zones where groundwater exchange would dominate — sampled to supply boundary fluxes, but inter-column exchange itself is NOT simulated.

validation_design.target_variable: hillslope-to-stream travel time / stream transit time
validation_design.observation_source: none provided in brief (no tracer / streamflow transit-time data in-domain)

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline uniform forcing (1980-2018 available), native soil sampled from raster per point

requires_capabilities.why: represent lateral flow and inter-hillslope groundwater exchange
compute hillslope-to-stream transit times along connected flowpaths
neighboring positions must share a water table to exchange groundwater
isolate topography-through-climate effects across the 352-1977 m range
define ridge/mid-slope/toe positions and flowpath connectivity for the expander
requires_capabilities.blocks: position-based stratification and any future routing topology

requires_capabilities.why: no in-domain observations to validate travel times

assumptions: Uniform baseline forcing across the domain (no elevation downscaling available).
Soil texture at each point is drawn from a gridded raster by the downstream expander.
The fallback 9-column set is a boundary-flux characterization only and must not be reported as travel times or lateral-exchange results.
No observations exist in-domain, so no quantitative validation is possible.
open_questions: Is there any in-domain streamflow, tracer, or well data that could later constrain transit times?
Should we invest in the ELM->PFLOTRAN coupler + routing solver, given travel times are the actual deliverable and are currently infeasible?
Preferred hillslope transect definition — synthetic representative hillslopes vs DEM-derived flowpaths?
